reproduction_target: Mechanistic variant-to-function study of the 9p21.3 CAD risk locus. The wet-lab half generates the primary evidence (chromatin/epigenome profiling of five primary human vascular wall cell types under five CAD-relevant stimulations, a densely tiled CRISPRi-MAC-seq screen over the 9p21.3 haplotype, siRNA knockdown with high-content LipocyteProfiler/fibroblast-activation imaging and RNA-seq, and a human LAD coronary artery single-nucleus multiome cohort). The computational reproduction target is the analysis half: (i) ChromHMM joint chromatin-state annotation of the vascular cell panel and the resulting novel-enhancer and super-enhancer calls (Fig. 1, Fig. S1); (ii) LDSC heritability partitioning and MAGMA gene prioritisation implicating vascular cell types and MTAP (Fig. 1, Fig. 3D-E, Fig. S8A); (iii) the CRISPRi-MAC-seq analysis chain - STARsolo counting, per-plate QC, per-plate z-scoring, and the 1000 bp/500 bp sliding-window permutation test at z = -1.96 that identifies the repressive enhancer windows (Fig. 2); (iv) the siMTAP LipocyteProfiler morphological pipeline (CellProfiler feature extraction, 3252 -> 850 feature reduction, inverse normal transformation, Wilcoxon/q-value testing, Morpheus clustering) and the siMTAP RNA-seq differential expression and GO network analysis (Figs. 4-5); (v) the human LAD snMultiome pipeline (Cell Ranger ARC, Demuxlet, Scrublet, Seurat/Harmony, ArchR, ArchR2Signac, CHOIR annotation, SCENT caQTL/enhancer-gene linkage) supporting the genotype-dependent MTAP regulation claim (Fig. 2E, Fig. 6); and (vi) the population-scale support analyses (FinnGen Olink, STARNET, DCM/HCM snRNA-seq re-analysis, FinnGen SuSiE fine-mapping).
granularity_note: Coarse one-step-per-named-tool/analysis-invocation, cut from the bioRxiv v1 JATS XML full text (fetched by curl from the .source.xml endpoint, HTTP 200, 304,822 bytes; title-phrase check 'Cell-State Transitions' present, so this is not a swapped fetch). Methods run from 'Data and Code Availability' to 'Cell Type-Specific Chromatin Accessibility QTL Analysis'. 39 computational steps (C1-C39) and 17 wet-lab steps (W1-W17). Steps were cut at named-tool granularity where the prose names a tool (Bowtie2, MACS3, ChromHMM, BEDTools, ROSE, LDSC, MAGMA, bcl2fastq, STARsolo, WASP, Eagle/PLINK/BCFtools, CellProfiler, Morpheus, Picard/Kallisto/tximport/DESeq2, gProfiler/igraph, Cell Ranger ARC, Demuxlet, Scrublet, Seurat/Harmony, ArchR, ArchR2Signac, CHOIR, SCENT) and at named-analysis granularity where it does not (haplotype enhancer annotation, MAC-seq batch correction + permutation window test, LipocyteProfiler feature reduction / INT / Wilcoxon). Revvity SImA image analysis is counted as a computational step (C39), not wet-lab, because it produces quantitative results reported in the paper. qPCR delta-delta-Ct quantification is left inside the wet-lab step W13 because it is a bench readout with no software artifact. Figure generation is not separately step-listed; plotting scripts for the deposited analyses live inside the corresponding C-steps, and no plotting tool is named for the remainder. Two prose facts recorded verbatim and not reconciled: (a) the Code Availability sentence is future-tense - 'Code used in all analyses will be made available and public on GitHub' - while one of the two named repositories is already public and populated and the other returns 404; (b) the siRNA RNA-seq was aligned by the Broad Genomics Platform against hg19 and then re-pseudo-aligned by the authors against hg38/Gencode v44, so two builds are in play in one chain.

steps.label: Alignment of vascular-cell Mint-ChIP histone (H3K4me1, H3K27ac, H3K4me3, H3K27me3) and ATAC reads to GRCh38 with Bowtie2. Methods verbatim: 'The preprocessing of the histone mark and ATAC signals included aligning to GRCh38 reference genome using Bowtie2'. No Bowtie2 version, no command line, no reference-build accession/checksum. The raw reads generated by this study have no GEO/SRA/ENA accession anywhere in the paper; Data and Code Availability states only that 'All data supporting findings from this study are included in the main figures of the manuscript as well as in the supplemental figures.' No alignment script is present in the deposited repository (https://github.com/MelinaClaussnitzerLab/V2F-9p21.3-CAD starts at peak filtering).

Peak calling on the aligned Mint-ChIP and ATAC signal with MACS3. Methods verbatim: 'calling peaks using MACS3 tools'. No MACS3 version, no q/p-value cutoff, no broad/narrow mode, no control/input specification, no command line. No peak-calling script in the repository; the repository's ChromHMM directory begins with filtering of already-called MACS peaks.

Low-confidence peak filtering with the study's own three criteria. Methods verbatim: 'Low-confidence peaks are characterized by any of the following criteria: (i) the fold-change at the peak summit is below the median of all fold-changes; (ii) the -10log10 P-value (display score) is lower than the 0.75 quantile of all peaks; or (iii) the P-value at the peak summit exceeds 0.05.' Code is deposited and exact: py_r_scripts/ChromHMM/000_filter_mintchip_macs_peaks.py and 001_filter_atac_macs_peaks.py. Blocked on data: the input MACS peak files are not deposited and have no accession. No Python version or dependency pin anywhere in the repository (no requirements.txt / environment.yml / Dockerfile / lockfile among the 102 deposited files).

ChromHMM joint chromatin-state modelling across five primary vascular cell types. Methods verbatim: 'We leveraged the ChromHMM method (version 1.22) for joint-modeling of chromatin states across the vascular cell types ... A joint model was subsequently trained on binarized peaks, utilizing a 200bp bin size.' Exact tool pin (1.22) and bin size given; the number of states and the state-emission seed are not stated, and state naming was manual ('Chromatin states were functionally annotated through manual examination'). Code deposited: 002_jointly_binarize_peaks.py, 003_jointly_model.py. Blocked on data (binarized peak inputs undeposited) and on version (tool pinned but no Java/Python/OS closure).

Identification of vascular-cell-specific enhancers by merging ChromHMM enhancer calls and intersecting against Roadmap enhancer annotations with BEDTools. Methods verbatim: 'BEDTools was used to merge the enhancer regions, and to intersect these regions with enhancer regions from the Roadmap project (annotated as genic enhancer1/2, active enhancer 1/2, or weak enhancer)'. Code deposited: postprocessin_enhancers/100_extract_roadmap_enhancers.py, 101_parse_chromHMM_JointModel_enhancers.py, 102_merge_and_intersect_bed_files.py, 103_extract_novel_chromhmm_enhancers.py. No BEDTools version, no overlap fraction (-f) or strand parameters, no Roadmap release identifier or download URL. Roadmap/ENCODE inputs are public but unpinned; the ChromHMM output half is undeposited.

Super-enhancer calling with the ROSE pipeline on basal H3K27ac signal. Methods verbatim: 'The ROSE pipeline was utilized to rank enhancer regions and identify potential super-enhancer regions ... The pipeline used H3K27ac signals from a whole-cell extract as the control.' Only the input-preparation script is deposited (ROSE/00_make_enhancer_gff_and_scripts.py); ROSE itself is an external pipeline cited by reference with no version, no stitching distance, no TSS-exclusion setting, and no invocation recorded.

Annotation of the 12 enhancers (E1-E12) within and around the 9p21.3 CAD haplotype. Methods verbatim: 'we intersected ChromHMM annotated enhancers along with ATAC-seq and H3K27ac ChIP-Seq data with with 50 coronary artery disease (CAD) 9p21.3 SNPs. We identified 12 enhancers spanning the 9p21.3 Haplotype'. The haplotype SNP table is deposited (Haplotypes.csv) and Table S2 gives HaploReg v4.2 provenance, but no script implements this intersection and no window/overlap rule is given for how an enhancer was assigned to the haplotype.

Stratified LD score regression (LDSC) heritability enrichment of cardiometabolic GWAS across vascular cell types, at basal state (top 10% t-statistic-ranked genes) and under stimulation (DEG sets). Methods verbatim: 'Genes were ranked by the absolute value of their t-statistics and we utilized top 10% expressed genes for heritability analysis ... we considered -log10 (p-adj) >= 3.35 as significant.' Gene-set construction code is deposited (LDSC_heritability/01_compute_tstat_genelist.py, 02_get_degs.ipynb, 03_dot_plot_DEG_hg38_basal_tstat_BC.R, 04_volcano_plot.py) but the LDSC run itself is externalised to an access-controlled Terra workflow: repo README verbatim 'Step 3: Run LDSC Heritability Terra workflow (https://app.terra.bio/#workspaces/claussnitzer-fdp/PRScs_MCL/workflows/ldsc_wf/ldsc_wf) on both the t-statics and DEG set for each cell-type'. No LDSC version, no baseline model version, no LD reference panel identifier. Input RNA-seq is in-house and undeposited; the GWAS summary statistics (CAD, ischemic stroke, total cholesterol, triglycerides, T2D, left-handedness, schizophrenia) are cited by reference only, with no accession or download URL.

MAGMA gene-based prioritisation of 9p21.3 candidate genes from CAD, T2D and SCZ GWAS summary statistics. Methods verbatim: 'Gene-based association analyses were performed with MAGMA v1.10 (Linux, GCC 5.2) that includes SNP annotation and gene-based analysis steps. SNP locations were annotated to NCBI gene coordinates using 1000 Genomes phase 3 reference pane (hg19 build), and gene-based statistics were computed using GWAS summary statistics with P-values and sample sizes.' Driver script and plotting notebook are deposited and exact (MAGMA_analysis/01_run_magma.sh, 02_9p21_MAGMA_results_plotting.ipynb) with a README giving the run order. Inputs are third-party public resources (published GWAS summary statistics + 1000G phase 3 panel) but are cited by reference/name rather than by accession, download URL or checksum, so data scores 1 rather than 2. Version is the exact pin MAGMA v1.10 with a compiler note but no environment closure - repo README Step 1 verbatim: 'Install Dependencies. See MAGMA github for instructions'. This is the only step in the paper whose four axes are all non-zero at prose level.

Design of the densely tiled 9p21.3 CRISPRi guide library with CRISPick. Methods verbatim: 'Guides targeting enhancer regions and variants were designed using CRISPick. For our densely tiled 9p21.3 library, 3-5 guides were generated for each of the 50 CAD risk SNPs within the haplotype, and 15 guides were generated for each of the 12 annotated enhancer regions. 36 locus-binding negative control guides ... near the 9p21.3 locus between coordinates Chr9:22174501-22175087 (hg38), were included ... 13 non-targeting guides ... (Table S6).' Guide counts and control coordinates are given and the final guide list is in Table S6, but CRISPick is a hosted Broad web service with no version, no run date, no parameter record (rule set, genome build, off-target filter) and no deposited design script.

MAC-seq BCL-to-FASTQ conversion and demultiplexing. Methods verbatim: 'After sequencing, the raw base-call (BCL) were demultiplexed using bcl2fastq (version 2.20) to generate FASTQ files.' Exact tool pin but no sample sheet, no barcode-mismatch setting, no deposited BCL/FASTQ (no SRA/ENA accession), and no script.

MAC-seq alignment and UMI counting with STARsolo. Methods verbatim gives the full command: 'FASTQs were then aligned to the reference human genome (GRCh38) using STARsolo (STAR version 2.7.10a) by specifying STAR --soloType CB_UMI_Simple --soloCBwhitelist [/path/to/barcodes.txt] --soloCBstart 1 --soloCBlen 10 --soloUMIstart 11 --soloUMIlen 16 --quantMode GeneCounts --soloFeatures Gene --readFilesCommand zcat. The reads were demultiplexed based on the MAC-seq well barcodes (Table S26)'. Params are essentially complete (full CLI + barcode table in supplement) and the STAR version is exactly pinned, but the FASTQs are undeposited, the GRCh38 index/GTF build is unnamed, the whitelist path is a placeholder, and no script or environment is deposited.

Per-plate MAC-seq QC: mitochondrial and ribosomal fraction per well, TPM normalisation, and cross-plate comparison of 9p21 gene expression in biological replicate plates (Figure S10). Sixteen exact QC scripts are deposited (MAC_Seq/plate_qc_scripts/2023_cfb_dxl05_qc.R through 2024_smc_dxl05_qc.R). Blocked on data (raw UMI count matrices are not deposited and have no accession) and on version (no R version, no package versions, no sessionInfo, no renv.lock in the repository).

MAC-seq batch correction and permutation-based sliding-window detection of repressive regions. Methods verbatim: 'expression of 9p21.3 genes were z-score normalized on a per-plate basis ... the locus was tiled into 1000-bp windows, staggered every 500bp for 50% overlap ... the labels of all guides were randomized, a permuted mean expression value was calculated, and this process was repeated for 500 total iterations ... A significance level of z-score =-1.96 was used to identify significantly repressed regions.' Parameters are fully specified and the code is deposited and exact (MAC_Seq/macseq_sliding_window_stats.R plus the seven-script cfb_final_analysis and smc_final_analysis series). Blocked on data (per-plate count matrices undeposited) and on version (no R or package version anywhere). No random seed is stated for the 500-iteration permutation.

Combined haplotype test on RNA profiles using the WASP pipeline, aggregated per gene and assessed by binomial test. Methods verbatim: 'Combined haplotype tests were performed on RNA profiles using the WASP analysis pipeline ... To determine the significance level of the analysis, a binomial test was conducted. This test compared the number of tested conditions against the number of significant tests (P-value< 0.05).' No WASP version, no configuration, no deposited script or wrapper, no input allelic-count data.

FinnGen Olink proteomics analysis of MTAP in the cardiovascular cohort. Methods verbatim: 'We investigated the Olink proteomics data (2025) from FinnGen. The population contains N=1,829 participants from which 1,624 were part of the cardiovascular disease cohort (FinnGen code: FG_CVD [https://r13.finngen.fi/pheno/FG_CVD]) ... MTAP Olink expression was then adjusted for age and sex ... Wilcox test was used to quantify the differences.' FinnGen individual-level Olink data is controlled-access via a documented application route (the endpoint browser URL resolves, HTTP 200), so data scores 1; no analysis script is deposited, no software/version is named for the adjustment or the test, and the covariate model form is described in prose only.

STARNET differential-expression query for the 9p21.3 genes. Methods verbatim: 'The STARNET portal (http://starnet.mssm.edu/) provides differential expression data for target genes, comparing CAD patients (N=600) with a control group (N=250). We utilized the portal to query the genes within the 9p21.3 locus; the log2 fold changes between the disease and control cases and their corresponding p-values were downloaded from the portal.' The portal is live (HTTP 200) but the data are hosted behind a mutable web interface with no snapshot date, no data version, no download record, no tissue selection stated, and no script.

Re-analysis of a published dilated/hypertrophic cardiomyopathy left-ventricle snRNA-seq dataset for 9p21.3 locus gene expression. Methods verbatim: 'we utilized data from a previous single-nucleus RNA sequencing study of left ventricle samples ... Gene expressions were normalized via log-transformation, and age and sex were regressed out. The residuals from this adjustment were then used for a non-parametric comparison of means ... we employed a Wilcoxon test. This analysis was performed on individual annotated cell types and repeated after pseudo-bulking the data.' Code is deposited (snRNA-seq_human_hearts/10_expressions.Rmd). The source dataset is cited by reference only with no accession, repository or access route named in this paper; no R or package versions are given.

Genotyping QC, phasing and imputation of the vascular cell lines. Methods verbatim: 'Vascular cell wall samples were sequenced using the Illumina Global Diversity Array (GDA), yielding 1,904,599 variants per sample ... the data underwent quality control, phasing (Eagle v2.4), and imputation using the TOPMed Imputation Server, based on the TOPMed r3 reference panel ... Variants with a minor allele frequency (MAF) of 0.001 or less and a Hardy-Weinberg equilibrium P-value of 1x10-20 - or less were removed using the PLINK tool set. Finally, the BCFtools was used to remove variants with R2 > 0.5, resulting in 7,854,254 variants.' Filter thresholds and the reference panel release are given; Eagle is pinned at v2.4 but PLINK and BCFtools carry no version and the TOPMed Imputation Server is a hosted, versionless external service. Genotype data are not deposited and have no accession. No script.

High-content image segmentation and feature extraction with CellProfiler on Terra. Methods verbatim: 'Quantitation was performed by running CellProfiler 4.2.6 on CellProfiler-on-Terra (https://github.com/broadinstitute/cellprofiler-on-Terra). Before segmentation, illumination correction was applied across each image channel (DNA, BODIPYRNA, AGP, Mito) ... Nuclei were identified using the HOECHST stain, and the watershed method was used to identify whole cells using the Phalloidin/WGA and BODIPY/SYTO14 stains.' Both CellProfiler pipeline definitions are deposited (LP_Morphology/0_cppipe/analysis.cppipe and illum.cppipe) so parameters are machine-readable, and CellProfiler is exactly pinned at 4.2.6; the CellProfiler-on-Terra WDL is referenced by bare repository URL with no commit or workflow version, and the raw Opera Phenix images are not deposited and have no accession.

LipocyteProfiler feature QC and redundancy reduction. Methods verbatim: 'One well with a total cell count of less than 9000 was removed in CFB ... Measurement categories known to be noisy, namely Manders, RWC, and Costes features, were removed. Additionally, features with zero standard deviation across all images, bounding box metrics, and X and Y coordinate features were removed. To reduce feature redundancy, we calculated the Pearson correlation (R2) for all feature pairs, creating a distance matrix with 1-R2. We then applied complete-linkage hierarchical clustering to this matrix, grouping features into 850 clusters from 3,252, each maintaining a minimum intracluster R2 of 0.9.' Both the code and its input are deposited (LP_Morphology/4_featureReduction/featureReduction.ipynb with raw_df.csv, plus 2_surveyCellCount/cellCount.R and wellQC.csv, plus the manual QC exclusions in Table S28), which is the strongest data+code position in the paper. Blocked solely on version: no Python/R version, no package versions, no lockfile, no sessionInfo anywhere in the repository.

Inverse normal transformation of the reduced morphological feature set. Methods verbatim: 'Signals were normalized using the inverse normal transformation (R's RankNorm) for downstream analysis.' Code and both input and output are deposited (LP_Morphology/5_inverseNormalTransformation/InverseNormalTransformation.R, data_.csv, cfb_int.csv, smc_int.csv). The RankNorm implementation is cited by reference but its package (RNOmni) is not named in prose, and no R or package version is given.

Wilcoxon rank-sum testing of siMTAP knockdown versus non-targeting control, with q-value adjustment. Methods verbatim: 'For each cell type, two pairwise comparisons were conducted: basal siMTAP vs. basal nontargeting control, and TGF-beta siMTAP vs. TGF-beta nontargeting control. Statistical significance for each normalized feature was determined using the Wilcoxon rank sum test (Mann-Whitney U), and raw p-values were adjusted to q-values using the q-value package (https://bioconductor.org/packages/release/bioc/html/qvalue.html).' Code and inputs deposited (LP_Morphology/6_wilcoxTestAndStackPlot/wilcox.R, stack.R, inverseNormalTransformed_cfb.csv, inverseNormalTransformed_smc.csv). The qvalue package is cited by a 'release' Bioconductor URL, which is a moving target with no version pin; no significance threshold on q is stated in prose.

Similarity-matrix construction and clustering of control versus siMTAP wells in Morpheus. Methods verbatim: 'A similarity matrix was then generated (using Morpheus) between all non-targeting control and siMTAP-knockdown wells.' Inputs and exported figures are deposited (LP_Morphology/7_Morpheus_Clustering/cfb_INT_pearson_avg_input.csv, smc_INT_pearson_avg_input.csv, CFB.pdf/svg, SMC.pdf/svg) and the repo README states 'Clustering heatmaps exported from Broad Institute's Morpheus software', but Morpheus is an interactive web tool: there is no script, no version, no saved session, and no linkage/metric setting recorded.

Pseudo-alignment of siRNA-knockdown RNA-seq to the transcriptome with Kallisto, after CRAM-to-FASTQ conversion with Picard. Methods verbatim: 'Sequencing data were initially processed by the Broad Genomics Platform (GP), where raw sequencing reads were aligned against the human genome (hg19) reference assembly and stored as CRAM files. Subsequently, CRAM files were converted back into FASTQ files using Picard (version 2.9.0, function: SamToFastq). Paired-end reads were then pseudo-aligned to the human transcriptome derived from the hg38 reference annotation (Gencode v44) using Kallisto (version 0.48.0).' Both tools and the annotation release are exactly pinned, but no script is deposited, the index-build command and bootstrap count are unstated, and the sequencing data have no accession.

Transcript-to-gene aggregation with tximport. Methods verbatim gives the exact call: 'The resulting transcript-level estimates were aggregated into gene-level counts using the tximport package in R [version 1.24.0, function tximport(fileList, type = "kallisto", tx2gene = tx2gene, ignoreAfterBar = T)].' Exact package pin and full call, but the tx2gene map construction is not described, no R version is given, and no script is deposited.

Differential gene expression for siRNA knockdowns with DESeq2. Methods verbatim: 'The gene-level count matrix was used for differential gene expression (DEG) analysis using the function DESeq() in DESeq2 (version 1.36.0). DEGs with adjusted P-value< 0.05 and |log2 fold change| >=1 were considered significantly DEGs between groups.' Exact package pin and explicit thresholds, but the design formula, the contrast specification and the shrinkage setting are unstated, no R version is given, no script is deposited, and the count matrix is not deposited.

Gene Ontology over-representation analysis of the knockdown DEGs with gProfiler. Methods verbatim: 'We performed gene ontology enrichment analysis for significant differentially expressed genes (P-adj<0.05) using over-representation analysis with the gProfiler tool.' No gProfiler/gprofiler2 version, no database release (g:Profiler versions its data by Ensembl release), no background gene set, no multiple-testing method, no script.

GO-term network construction and Leiden clustering of the enrichment results. Methods verbatim: 'creating a weighted network of these enriched GO terms by establishing edges between terms based on shared genes, using the Jaccard similarity measure ... The network was then clustered using the Leiden algorithm ... The network analysis and visualization was implemented using R package igraph (v2.1.4) ... only parent GO nodes were included in the network representation when all parent and corresponding child terms were present in the list.' igraph is exactly pinned but the Leiden implementation and its resolution parameter, the Jaccard edge threshold and the random seed are all unstated, and no script is deposited.

9p21.3 statistical fine-mapping for the FinnGen 'Coronary revascularization (ANGIO or CABG)' endpoint. Methods verbatim: 'Fine-mapped data from FinnGen for the trait "Coronary revascularization (ANGIO or CABG)" ... were accessed from the FinnGen browser (https://r12.finngen.fi/region/I9_REVASC/9:21900177-22300177). Briefly, in-sample dosage LD was calculated using LDStore2 and then finemapping was conducted using SuSiE with in-sample dosage LD and GWAS summary statistics as input.' The fine-mapping was performed by FinnGen, not by the authors; the browser URL resolves (HTTP 200) and the release is identifiable (r12), but no LDStore2 or SuSiE version, no credible-set parameters (L, coverage) and no download record are given, and the in-sample LD is not accessible outside FinnGen.

Human LAD coronary artery snMultiome read mapping and quantification with Cell Ranger ARC. Methods verbatim: 'Read mapping and quantification were performed using Cell Ranger ARC (version 2.0.1).' Exact tool pin, but no reference package version, no command line, no libraries CSV. The code for this entire arm of the paper is claimed at https://github.com/Antidington/LAD_phase1_9p21, which returns HTTP 404 (the GitHub account exists; the repository does not resolve). The sequencing data have no accession and the tissue is human-subject material collected under IRB at Zhongnan Hospital of Wuhan University, so raw data would in any case require a controlled-access route that the paper does not describe.

Donor demultiplexing of the snMultiome BAMs and genotype imputation. Methods verbatim: 'Donor demultiplexing was executed with Demuxlet v2 (https://github.com/statgen/demuxlet) on the alignment files (BAM format) from both snRNA-seq and snATAC-seq data. This process utilized genotyping information from each donor's Illumina Infinium Asian Screening Array, which was processed into VCF files imputed either by minimac3 or via the Michigan Imputation Server (https://imputationserver.sph.umich.edu).' 'Demuxlet v2' is a coarse major-version reference with no commit; minimac3 has no version; the imputation route is stated as an either/or, so which panel produced which donor's VCF is not recoverable. No code (repository 404), no donor genotypes deposited.

Doublet removal and multiome quality control. Methods verbatim: 'Doublets were identified and removed using Scrublet v0.2.3. Data quality control criteria were applied as follows: for the snRNA-seq dataset, we filtered cells with parameters nCount_RNA > 200, nFeature_RNA > 200, and the mitochondrial gene percentage < 10%; for the snATAC-seq dataset, we filtered cells whose TSS enrichment score > 2 and the number of fragments > 1000.' Thresholds are complete and Scrublet is exactly pinned, but no expected-doublet-rate or seed is given, no code is available (repository 404), and the count matrices are not deposited.

snRNA-seq processing with Seurat and batch correction with Harmony. Methods verbatim: 'We used Seurat v5 ... (1) Count matrix was normalized using the NormalizeData function (with normalization.method = "LogNormalize" and scale.factor = 10^4), (2) Top 2,000 highly variable genes were calculated using the FindVariableFeatures function (with selection.method = "vst"), (3) PCA was performed using ScaleData and PCA functions with default parameters. (4) Batch effect was removed using the RunHarmony function (with parameters max_iter = 50 and early_stop = TRUE) implemented in Harmony v1.2.3 ... (5) For visualization, the RunUMAP function was applied to the top 30 PCs.' Function-level parameters are unusually complete; Harmony is exactly pinned but 'Seurat v5' is a major-version reference only (v5.0.x through v5.3.x differ), and no R version is given. No code (repository 404), no data.

snATAC-seq processing with ArchR. Methods verbatim: 'We used ArchR v1.0.3 ... (1) Tile matrix was generated using the addTileMatrix (tile size 500bp), used by ArchR to quantify chromatin accessibility. (2) The dimensionality reduction was conducted using a latent semantic indexing algorithm, and the top 25,000 variable bins ranked by signal variance were selected as input, (3) Batch effects were removed using addHarmony, (4) UMAP was generated from the 30 dimensions.' Exact tool pin and explicit parameters; iterative-LSI iteration count and seed are unstated. No code (repository 404), no fragment files deposited.

Multiome integration: conversion of the ArchR project and Seurat object into a Signac object and weighted-nearest-neighbour joint embedding. Methods verbatim: 'we converted the processed ArchR project and Seurat object into a uniform Signac object using ArchR2Signac v1.0.5 (https://github.com/swaruplabUCI/ArchRtoSignac). We then computed a joint neighbour graph that represents both gene expression and chromatin accessibility using the weighted nearest-neighbour method in Seurat. We plotted the joint UMAP embedding with RunUMAP.' ArchR2Signac is exactly pinned but Signac itself is not versioned and the WNN call parameters (reduction list, dims, k.nn) are not given. No code (repository 404), no intermediate objects deposited.

Cell-type annotation with CHOIR. Methods verbatim: 'we applied CHOIR v0.3.0 (https://github.com/corceslab/CHOIR), which employs random forest classifiers in combination with permutation testing throughout a hierarchical clustering tree for the annotation ... By following the instructions provided by CHOIR, we yielded 20 robust clusters. Three clusters with high expression of fibroblast markers (DCN, LUM, COL3A1, and LAMA2) were merged and collectively annotated as fibroblasts, and one cluster was annotated as smooth muscle cells according to markers ACTA2, MYH11, MYL9, and TAGLN.' Exact tool pin and marker-based merge rule are given, but the CHOIR call parameters and the random seed for the random-forest permutation testing are not, so cluster identity is not deterministically recoverable. No code (repository 404), no data.

Cell-type-specific chromatin accessibility QTL analysis linking 9p21.3 enhancers to target genes with SCENT. Methods verbatim: 'we initially grouped cells by their rs1537371 genotypes (CC, CA, and AA) into three categories. Next, we utilized SCENT v1.0.1 (https://github.com/immunogenomics/SCENT) to connect enhancers to target genes. We used the getMatrixFromProject function (with parameters useMatrix = "TileMatrix" and binarize = TRUE) to build the input cell-by-tile matrix ... we filtered tiles that were opened or genes expressed in at least 0.1% of cells for each group. Then, we performed SCENT on each 9p21.3 tile-gene pair using the SCENT algorithm (with regr = "poisson" and bin = FALSE). To account for potential confounders, this analysis was adjusted for sample ID, age, mitochondrial gene percentage, log-transformed number of counts, TSS enrichment score, and log-transformed number of fragments.' Parameters and covariates are essentially complete and SCENT is exactly pinned; the bootstrap count and seed are unstated. No code (repository 404), no data.

Fibroblast-activation image analysis in Revvity Signal Image Artist (SImA). Methods verbatim: 'For the fibroblast activation stain, image analysis was performed in Revvity's Signal Image Artists (SImA) software. Single nuclei were identified by Hoechst signal, and cell bodies were thresholded using a composite COL1a1 and alpha-tubulin signal ... alphaSMA fibers were additionally identified by thresholding the alphaSMA stain channel for all regions with an intensity value of over 1500.' One threshold is given, but SImA is closed commercial GUI software with no version stated, no exported analysis definition deposited, and the raw images are not deposited. Recorded as a computational step (it produces quantitative results reported in the paper), not as wet-lab.

Sourcing and maintenance of primary and immortalised vascular cells: atrial fibroblast (Lonza CC-2903), ventricular fibroblast (Lonza CC-2904), coronary artery endothelial cells (Lonza CC-2585), pulmonary artery SMC (Lonza CC-2581), coronary artery SMC (Lonza CC-2583), adipose-derived microvascular pericytes (Angioproteomie cAP-0043), vascular fibroblasts (Cell Systems ACBRI 5118), coronary artery SMC (ATCC PCS-100-021), immortalised fibroblast (ABM T0446) and coronary artery SMC (ABM T0557); culture in Lonza FGM-3, SmGM-2, EGM and Creative Bioarray CM-C12030Z.

CAD disease-relevant stimulation panel: low serum (5% FBS), oxLDL (100 ug/mL in 5% FBS), IL-1alpha (10 ng/uL), IL-6 (20 ng/uL) + TNFalpha (10 ng/uL), and high glucose (25 mM), two replicates per condition, in 6-well plates with stated seeding densities.
Mint-ChIP histone-mark profiling (H3K4me1, H3K27ac, H3K4me3, H3K27me3) of the stimulated and basal vascular cells.
ATAC-seq library preparation on the same stimulated and basal vascular cells.
Generation of constitutively expressing dCas9-KRAB CRISPRi cell lines by lentiviral spinfection (930 x g, 150 min, polybrene 10 ug/mL) and hygromycin selection (50 ug/mL, 5-8 days).
CRISPRi activity assay with Cellecta CRISPRiTest dCas9-Repressor kit, GFP/RFP ratio read on a CytoFLEX S and gated in FlowJo.

Lentivirus production (HEK293T, psPAX2 #12259, VSVG, TransIT-LT1) and transduction of the densely tiled 9p21.3 sgRNA library produced by the Broad Genomic Perturbation Platform in arrayed 96-well format.

MAC-seq library construction (96 barcodes, SPRIselect beads, Covaris LE220Rsc sonication at 200 W / 25% duty / 50 cycles-per-burst / 85 s) and sequencing on NextSeq2000 P3-100 at 750 pM with a 0.3 uM custom read-1 primer.
siRNA knockdown of MTAP, DMRTA1, CDKN2A, CDKN2B, MIR31HG and CDKN2B-AS1 (Dharmacon SMARTpools, 50 nM, DharmaFECT 1) with and without 80 ng/mL TGF-beta, in 96-well PhenoPlates.
LipocyteProfiler and fibroblast-activation staining panels (4% PFA / 0.5% Triton-X 100 fixation) and confocal imaging on a Perkin Elmer Opera Phenix.
RNA extraction (Qiagen RNeasy Plus Mini), QC on NanoDrop2000, and RNA-seq library preparation/sequencing of the siRNA-treated fibroblasts and SMCs by the Broad Genomics Platform.
Western blot for dCas9-KRAB expression (Diagenode C15310258) with GAPDH loading control (CST 5174S).
qPCR validation of siRNA and CRISPRi efficiency (Power SYBR Green / Cells-to-Ct, BioRad CFX Opus 384, 2^-ddCt normalised to TBP, primers in Table S29).

Collection of human left anterior descending coronary artery segments from explanted hearts at Zhongnan Hospital of Wuhan University under IRB-approved protocols with written informed consent; cardioplegic arrest, dissection on ice, snap-freezing in liquid nitrogen.
Nuclei isolation and formaldehyde fixation from frozen LAD tissue (Dounce homogenisation in 0.1x lysis buffer, 70 um and 40 um straining, 1.5% formaldehyde).

10x Chromium Next GEM Single Cell Multiome ATAC + Gene Expression library construction by the UDA-seq post-indexing method (300,000 nuclei per channel, 96-well post-indexing, KAPA HiFi ATAC enrichment) and sequencing on MGISeq-T7 (ATAC 100 bp PE, 20,000 reads/cell; RNA 150 bp PE, 50,000 reads/cell).
Genotyping of the vascular cell wall samples on the Illumina Global Diversity Array (1,904,599 variants per sample) and of the LAD donors on the Illumina Infinium Asian Screening Array.

headline.static_readiness: 0/39 (0%) - stage1 ceiling only, no R-star (R-star needs stage-2 code verification). Unexecuted; no declared environment exists to be statically validated, let alone verified as the environment that produced the results. n_exact_capture_unexecuted = 0, n_fetch_required = 0.
headline.inference_inclusive_upper_bound: 1/39 (2.6%) at Stage 1. Exactly one computational step - C9, the MAGMA gene-based analysis - has all four axes non-zero and therefore reaches the Stage-1 RI ceiling; the other 38 cap at NI. The binding constraint is data, not code. The paper deposits no accession of any kind: Data and Code Availability states in full that 'All data supporting findings from this study are included in the main figures of the manuscript as well as in the supplemental figures', and no GEO, SRA, ENA, ArrayExpress, dbGaP, EGA, figshare or Zenodo identifier appears anywhere in the text. Every dataset this study generated - Mint-ChIP and ATAC libraries across five vascular cell types and five stimulations, the CRISPRi-MAC-seq screen, the siRNA RNA-seq, the Opera Phenix image sets, the GDA genotypes, and the human LAD coronary artery snMultiome - is therefore unavailable, which zeroes the data axis on 30 of 39 steps regardless of how good the code is. The code axis is genuinely split in two. One repository (https://github.com/MelinaClaussnitzerLab/V2F-9p21.3-CAD) is live, public, MIT-licensed, 102 files, last pushed 2025-11-18 (preprint day), and it covers the ChromHMM chain, the enhancer post-processing, LDSC gene-set construction, MAGMA, the full MAC-seq QC and sliding-window analysis (23 R scripts), the LipocyteProfiler morphology chain including CellProfiler .cppipe pipelines and several intermediate CSVs, and the cardiomyopathy snRNA-seq re-analysis - 14 steps score code=2. The other (https://github.com/Antidington/LAD_phase1_9p21) returns HTTP 404, and with it the entire human LAD snMultiome arm (C31-C38, eight steps) has no code at all. Version is the second hard wall and is the reason the three strongest steps miss RI: C21, C22 and C23 have data=2 (inputs deposited in the repo), code=2 and params=2, and fail only because no interpreter or package version is recorded - the repository contains no requirements.txt, environment.yml, Dockerfile, conda spec, renv.lock, sessionInfo output or any other lock among its 102 files, and no README states one. Prose pins are real but partial: 18 tools carry exact versions (ChromHMM 1.22, bcl2fastq 2.20, STAR 2.7.10a, MAGMA v1.10, Eagle v2.4, CellProfiler 4.2.6, Picard 2.9.0, Kallisto 0.48.0, tximport 1.24.0, DESeq2 1.36.0, igraph v2.1.4, Cell Ranger ARC 2.0.1, Scrublet v0.2.3, Harmony v1.2.3, ArchR v1.0.3, ArchR2Signac v1.0.5, CHOIR v0.3.0, SCENT v1.0.1) while Bowtie2, MACS3, BEDTools, ROSE, LDSC, WASP, PLINK, BCFtools, minimac3, gProfiler, the Leiden implementation, the qvalue package, Morpheus, SImA, R itself and Python itself carry none; 'Seurat v5' and 'Demuxlet v2' are major-version references only. Params is the paper's strongest axis - the full STARsolo command line, the exact tximport call, the DESeq2 thresholds, the permutation window geometry (1000 bp / 500 bp stagger / 500 iterations / z = -1.96), the multiome QC cutoffs and the SCENT covariate list are all in prose - but no random seed is stated for any of the stochastic procedures (the 500-iteration permutation test, Scrublet, UMAP, Harmony, Leiden, the CHOIR random-forest permutation testing). Because the top Stage-1 verdict is capped at RI, 1/39 is a ceiling and not a claim that C9 was reproduced.
headline.coverage: 39 computational steps assessed (S = 39) against 17 wet-lab steps (W = 17); computational coverage = 39/56 = 70%% of the enumerated Methods steps. This is a mixed wet-lab/computational paper: the wet-lab steps are out of scope for computational reproduction (gap type 10) and are enumerated only so the denominator is not mistaken for the whole paper. Within the computational half, coverage is itself asymmetric between the two code repositories: 14 of 39 steps (C3, C4, C5, C9, C13, C14, C18, C20, C21, C22, C23, plus partial credit on C6 and C8) are backed by deposited exact code in the live repository, while the eight steps of the human LAD snMultiome arm (C31-C38) are backed by a repository URL that does not resolve. The Terra-hosted LDSC workflow (C8) and the TOPMed Imputation Server (C19) externalise sub-pipelines to services the reader cannot enter, and CRISPick (C10), Morpheus (C24), SImA (C39) and the STARNET portal (C17) are versionless interactive or proprietary tools.
